description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md to discover the exact nvidia-smi CLI flags: '-L' for listing GPUs, '-q -d MEMORY,POWER' for filtered queries, and '--query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv' for process reporting. Generic agents may try '--query-gpu' or other wrong flags. (2) Write audit_gpus.sh combining all three nvidia-smi invocations and redirecting the compute-apps CSV output to process_report.csv. (3) Write gpu_health_report.py using pynvml with the exact API: nvmlInit(), nvmlDeviceGetCount(), nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(i), nvmlDeviceGetName(handle).decode('utf-8'), nvmlDeviceGetTemperature(handle, pynvml.NVML_TEMPERATURE_GPU), nvmlDeviceGetPowerUsage(handle) / 1000.0 (critical mW->W conversion from SKILL.md), nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(handle) with .used // 1024**2 for MB, nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates(handle).gpu. The key proprietary traps are: (a) power must be divided by 1000 to convert mW to W — failure means power_critical flag will never trigger correctly since raw values are ~312000-398000 mW; (b) NVML_TEMPERATURE_GPU constant as the second argument to GetTemperature; (c) .decode('utf-8') on the bytes name. The memory_critical threshold (>90%) catches GPU 1 at 97.5% usage, while power_critical (>390W) catches GPU 1 at 398W.
